LESSON: VIRTUES IN ISLAM

Grade: Grade 9
Subject: ISLAMIC RELIGIOUS EDUCATION
Strand: Akhlaq (Moral Teachings)
Topic 5.1: Virtues in Islam

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Virtues in Islam. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: Why is it important for Muslims to practise virtues?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. explain Islamic teachings on observing modesty, contentment, and trustworthiness in fulfilment of Allah (S.W.T.)’s commandments
2. describe ways in which Muslims can practise modesty, contentment, and trustworthiness as part of faith
3. practise modesty, contentment, and trustworthiness in day-to-day life to earn rewards from Allah (S.W.T.)
4. value modesty, contentment, and trustworthiness for a morally upright society

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: VIRTUES IN ISLAM
Subject: ISLAMIC RELIGIOUS EDUCATION · Grade: Grade 9
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Virtues in Islam helps you succeed in ISLAMIC RELIGIOUS EDUCATION. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

KEY FACTS: VIRTUES IN ISLAM
Study Virtues in Islam like a learner textbook page: meaning → examples → practice → check.
Replace teacher words with your own words.
If a step is unclear, rewrite it shorter and try again.

PART 1: Explain Islamic teachings on observing modesty, contentment, and trustworthiness in fulfilment of Allah (S.W.T.)’s commandments

What this means
In this part you learn to explain Islamic teachings on observing modesty, contentment, and trustworthiness in fulfilment of Allah (S.W.T.)’s commandments. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: explain Islamic teachings on observing modesty, contentment, and trustworthiness in fulfilment of Allah (S.W.T.)’s commandments.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Value in action: Show how “Virtues in Islam” looks when you treat a classmate kindly.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can explain Islamic teachings on observing modesty, contentment, and trustworthiness in fulfilment of Allah (S.W.T.)’s commandments. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Describe ways in which Muslims can practise modesty, contentment, and trustworthiness as part of faith

What this means
In this part you learn to describe ways in which Muslims can practise modesty, contentment, and trustworthiness as part of faith. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: describe ways in which Muslims can practise modesty, contentment, and trustworthiness as part of faith.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Story link: Retell a short faith/values story connected to Virtues in Islam in your own words.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can describe ways in which Muslims can practise modesty, contentment, and trustworthiness as part of faith. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Practise modesty, contentment, and trustworthiness in day-to-day life to earn rewards from Allah (S.W.T.)

What this means
In this part you learn to practise modesty, contentment, and trustworthiness in day-to-day life to earn rewards from Allah (S.W.T.). You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: practise modesty, contentment, and trustworthiness in day-to-day life to earn rewards from Allah (S.W.T.).
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Daily habit: Choose one good action to practise today because of this lesson.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can practise modesty, contentment, and trustworthiness in day-to-day life to earn rewards from Allah (S.W.T.). Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 4: Value modesty, contentment, and trustworthiness for a morally upright society

What this means
In this part you learn to value modesty, contentment, and trustworthiness for a morally upright society. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: value modesty, contentment, and trustworthiness for a morally upright society.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Value in action: Show how “Virtues in Islam” looks when you treat a classmate kindly.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can value modesty, contentment, and trustworthiness for a morally upright society. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Virtues in Islam is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Show how “Virtues in Islam” looks when you treat a classmate kindly. (skill: explain Islamic teachings on observing modesty, contentment, and trustworthiness in fulfilment of Allah (S.W.T.)’s commandments)

Example 2: Retell a short faith/values story connected to Virtues in Islam in your own words. (skill: describe ways in which Muslims can practise modesty, contentment, and trustworthiness as part of faith)

Example 3: Choose one good action to practise today because of this lesson. (skill: practise modesty, contentment, and trustworthiness in day-to-day life to earn rewards from Allah (S.W.T.))

Example 4: Show how “Virtues in Islam” looks when you treat a classmate kindly. (skill: value modesty, contentment, and trustworthiness for a morally upright society)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Virtues in Islam to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: explain Islamic teachings on observing modesty, contentment, and trustworthiness in fulfilment of Allah (S.W.T.)’s commandments.
3. Practise this skill: describe ways in which Muslims can practise modesty, contentment, and trustworthiness as part of faith.
4. Practise this skill: practise modesty, contentment, and trustworthiness in day-to-day life to earn rewards from Allah (S.W.T.).
5. Make one local Kenya example of Virtues in Islam from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Virtues in Islam: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 9 learner study Virtues in Islam?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Why is it important for Muslims to practise virtues?
2. How can a Muslim student exercise contentment in his life?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Virtues in Islam means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: explain Islamic teachings on observing modesty, contentment, and trustworthiness in fulfilment of Allah (S.W.T.)’s commandments.
5. Be able to: describe ways in which Muslims can practise modesty, contentment, and trustworthiness as part of faith.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
